content.title: John Calipari officially hired as Arkansas basketball coach
content.text: SportsUpdated: Apr. 10, 2024, 9:24 a.m.Published: Apr. 10, 2024, 9:22 a.m.John Calipari was officially named head basketball coach at Arkansas on Wednesday after 15 seasons at Kentucky. (AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar)APBy Creg Stephenson | cstephenson@al.comJohn Calipari has officially been hired as Arkansas head men’s basketball coach, jumping from Kentucky in one of the more notable coaching moves in recent years.The 65-year-old Calipari won 410 games in 15 seasons with the Wildcats, with six SEC championships, four Final Four berths and the 2012 NCAA tournament title. But he had fallen out of favor in Lexington, failing to get out of the first round of the NCAA tournament in two of the last three years and having not won an SEC regular-season or tournament championship since 2020.At Arkansas, Calipari — a 2015 inductee into the Basketball Hall of Fame — replaces Eric Musselman, who left last week to take the USC job. The Razorbacks went 16-17 in 2023-24, snapping a three-year run in which they advanced twice to the NCAA tournament Elite Eight and once to the Sweet 16.“By all accounts, John Calipari is one of the premier coaches in college basketball,” Arkansas athletics director Hunter Yurachek said. “A national championship coach, a four-time national coach of the year and one of the nation’s top recruiters, Coach Cal has consistently demonstrated his ability to attract outstanding talent and build championship teams within the Southeastern Conference and position his programs among the best in the nation.“As I visited with Coach Calipari during this process, he acknowledged the tremendous opportunity we have at the University of Arkansas to attract and retain top players and compete for championships. He understands the deep passion of the Razorback Nation and has experienced the tremendous home court advantage of Bud Walton Arena. I have no doubt that under Coach Calipari’s leadership and with the collective support of all those who love the Hogs, Razorback Basketball will continue to maintain its national prominence within college basketball.”In 32 seasons as a college head coach at UMass, Memphis and Kentucky, Calipari has won 813 games, with six trips to the Final Four, 16 conference regular-season championships and 15 conference tournament titles. Known as one of the top recruiters in the country, he has coached 40 players who went on to be first-round NBA draft picks (with two and possibly three more this year).Calipari announced his resignation from Kentucky on Tuesday, saying the Wildcats “need to hear another voice.” He is expected to remain one of the highest-paid coaches in college basketball at Arkansas, agreeing to a 5-year contract that will pay him $7 million per year.RECOMMENDEDJohn Calipari has signed a five-year contract with a salary beginning at $7 million/season. The contract has a maximum of two automatic rollover years for NCAA Tournament appearances that would extend the contract to 2031. He gets a $1 million signing bonus. He also has retention…— Brandon Marcello (@bmarcello) April 10, 2024 Though Arkansas has not been to a Final Four since 1995, the Razorbacks are one of three SEC teams with a national championship, winning the title under Nolan Richardson in 1994. Kentucky (8) and Florida (2) are the other SEC programs to win the NCAA tournament title.Attention now turns to Kentucky, which is reportedly pursuing Baylor’s Scott Drew to be its next head coach. Other names most often mentioned as candidates for the Wildcats are Connecticut two-time national champion Dan Hurley and Chicago Bulls coach Billy Donovan (a former Florida head coach and Kentucky assistant).
